candidates.summary: South Korea's Supreme Court overturned former prime minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence in the case concerning his role in the December 2024 martial-law declaration and sent the case back to the Seoul High Court. The court extended his detention by two months; the reversal did not result in his release.
candidates.title: South Korean Supreme Court overturns Han Duck-soo sentence and orders further proceedings

candidates.summary: South Korea's Supreme Court upheld former first lady Kim Keon Hee's four-year prison sentence and 50 million won fine for stock-price manipulation and accepting luxury gifts from the Unification Church. It dismissed appeals from both Kim and prosecutors and maintained her acquittal on a separate charge involving free opinion-poll results.
candidates.title: South Korean Supreme Court confirms Kim Keon Hee's four-year prison sentence

candidates.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump held bilateral talks in Shenzhen during the APEC summit. According to Xinhua's account reported by Reuters, they agreed to formulate an action plan for their bilateral relationship. Xi urged Washington to handle Taiwan appropriately to avoid setbacks and called for stronger communication on artificial-intelligence safety.
candidates.title: Xi and Trump meet in Shenzhen; Chinese account reports agreement to develop bilateral action plan

candidates.summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held trilateral talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. During the opening exchanges, Trump called for discussions on reducing nuclear weapons and referred to efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Putin said Ukraine had been a major focus of his earlier bilateral talks with Trump. No agreement on ending the war was announced in those exchanges.
candidates.title: Trump, Xi and Putin hold trilateral talks on Ukraine and nuclear arms

candidates.summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin concluded trilateral talks in Shenzhen and issued a declaration supporting dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, UN reform, increased refined-petroleum production and respect for state officials' immunities. The declaration contained no specific nuclear-arms reductions or timetable for negotiations and did not propose settlements for the wars in Ukraine or Iran.
candidates.title: Trump, Xi and Putin conclude summit with declaration but no specific arms-reduction agreement
candidates.geography: China; United States; Russia; Ukraine; Iran

sources.name: The National — declaration text published by Chinese state media

candidates.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in northern Rakhine State and failed to prevent and punish genocide. It ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those responsible, facilitate safe and voluntary returns, restore property and provide compensation. The judgment concerns Myanmar's responsibility as a state, not individual criminal convictions.
candidates.title: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar responsible for genocide against Rohingya

sources.name: International Court of Justice — press release hosted by UNHCR Refworld
UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar

candidates.summary: European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed that AI tools were used in a cyberattack first detected on October 22. Several applications were temporarily taken offline, and most had since been restored. Regnier said investigators had not detected evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole. He did not identify the attacker. The November 19 development was the public confirmation, not the attack's onset.
candidates.title: European Commission confirms AI-assisted October cyberattack

candidates.summary: The Labor Department reported that seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims rose by 1,000 to 203,000 for the week ending November 14. The previous week's figure was revised upward to 202,000. Continuing claims increased by 70,000 to 1,763,000 for the week ending November 7. These are figures released November 19, not claims filed solely that day.
candidates.title: US weekly initial unemployment claims rise to 203,000

candidates.summary: Anthropic shares began trading on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT at $111.50, above the $83 offering price set November 18. The offering comprised 980 million shares sold by the company and existing shareholders, totaling approximately $81.3 billion. Anthropic's pricing announcement said the offering was expected to close November 20, subject to customary conditions.
candidates.title: Anthropic shares begin Nasdaq trading above offering price

candidates.summary: Anthropic shares finished their first Nasdaq trading day at $97.17, 17.1% above the $83 offering price set November 18. The offering comprised 980 million shares sold by the company and existing shareholders, totaling approximately $81.3 billion. Anthropic's pricing announcement said closing was expected November 20, subject to customary conditions.
candidates.title: Anthropic closes first Nasdaq trading day 17.1% above offering price

candidates.summary: The Senate rejected H.Con.Res.93, a resolution directing removal of U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran, by 48–51. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul supported it; Democrat John Fetterman opposed it. The House had passed the measure in September. The vote did not change U.S. military authority or end the conflict.
candidates.title: Senate rejects Iran war-powers resolution by 48–51

sources.name: United States Senate Periodical Press Gallery

candidates.summary: The administration auctioned two 20-year offshore mineral lease areas near American Samoa. According to the Marine Minerals Administration, Wetstone U.S. Ventures submitted the only bids and won each area for the $3 million minimum. The leases permit preliminary activities, not immediate commercial mineral harvesting, which requires further approvals. Three lawsuits challenge the sales or the government's authority to conduct them.
candidates.title: American Samoa offshore mineral lease auction draws $6 million in winning bids

candidates.summary: The S&P 500 fell 147.80 points, or 2%, to 7,175.83, recording its sixth consecutive decline and longest losing streak since 2024. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.2%, to 49,097.06, and the Nasdaq composite lost 550.69 points, or 2.3%, to 23,879.20. More than 90% of S&P 500 constituents declined.
candidates.title: US stock indexes fall as S&P 500 extends losing streak to six sessions

candidates.summary: The Senate passed H.R.2347, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, by 62–33. The bill would shorten federal environmental-review deadlines, accelerate transmission development, limit some permit challenges and require large AI data centers to cover more associated grid-upgrade costs. Supporters said it would ease infrastructure bottlenecks; opponents raised concerns about environmental protections and tribal consultation. The amended measure goes to the House and was not law at the end of the coverage window.
candidates.title: Senate passes energy and infrastructure permitting bill by 62–33

sources.name: United States Senate Periodical Press Gallery
Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works

candidates.summary: The Army announced that controlled detonations of deteriorating lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown would be postponed from November 20 to November 23. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said the delay would allow additional public communication but that a forecast temperature drop risked further destabilizing the material. Environmental groups filed an emergency motion challenging the EPA disposal permit, arguing that the blasts could disperse toxic lead dust. The announcement postponed the operation; no detonation occurred in this development.
candidates.title: Army postpones planned destruction of deteriorating explosives in Iowa

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson issued a preliminary injunction restricting Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins's religious messages to employees through her official account. The judge found that messages assuming employees shared her Christian beliefs likely violated the First Amendment. The ruling did not restrict Rollins's private religious expression. USDA said it was evaluating its options, including a prompt appeal.
candidates.title: Judge restricts agriculture secretary's religious emails to employees

candidates.summary: President Donald Trump announced a posthumous pardon for Pete Rose's federal tax crimes. Rose pleaded guilty in 1990 to two charges of filing false tax returns and served five months in prison. The pardon is separate from Major League Baseball's decision in 2025 to remove Rose from its permanently ineligible list and does not itself induct him into the Baseball Hall of Fame.
candidates.title: Trump announces posthumous pardon for Pete Rose's tax crimes

candidates.summary: The Treasury Department imposed sanctions on the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang, Italy-based 'Ndrangheta and associated people and businesses. Treasury accused the networks of supporting international drug trafficking and money laundering. OFAC also issued a general license authorizing specified wind-down transactions involving certain newly blocked persons.
candidates.title: US sanctions Comanchero and 'Ndrangheta networks over alleged drug trafficking
candidates.geography: United States; Australia; Italy; Canada; New Zealand

sources.name: United States Department of the Treasury

candidates.summary: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that a Russian ballistic-missile attack struck three Dnipro River bridges, killed three people and injured about 15. He reported closures or traffic restrictions at the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Pivdennyi crossings. Reuters reported hearing explosions but could not independently confirm the officials' accounts. The attack occurred early November 20 in Kyiv, during the evening of November 19 in New York.
candidates.title: Kyiv mayor reports three killed as Russian missiles strike river bridges
